(Lexington, North Carolina) | college = [[Clemson Tigers football|Clemson]] | draftyear = 1982 | draftround = 1 | draftpick = 19 | teams = * [[Buffalo Bills]] ({{NFL Year|1982}}–{{NFL Year|1983}}) * [[Atlanta Falcons]] ({{NFL Year|1984}}) * [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] (1984) * [[Winnipeg Blue Bombers]] ({{CFL Year|1986}}–{{CFL Year|1991}}) | highlights = * 2× [[Grey Cup]] champion ([[76th Grey Cup|1988]], [[78th Grey Cup|1990]]) * [[College football national championships in NCAA Division I FBS|National champion]] ([[1981 Clemson Tigers football team|1981]]) * 2× First-team [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference football teams|All-ACC]] ([[1980 All-Atlantic Coast Conference football team|1980]], [[1981 All-Atlantic Coast Conference football team|1981]]) | statlabel1 = [[Reception (gridiron football)|Receptions]] | statvalue1 = 25 | statlabel2 = Receiving yards | statvalue2 = 375 | statlabel3 = Receiving [[touchdown]]s | statvalue3 = 3 | pfr = TuttPe00 }} '''Perry Tuttle''' (born August 2, 1959) is an American former professional [[gridiron football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was a national champion and [[Clemson football]] standout in the early 1980s. His career continued into the NFL ([[Buffalo Bills]], [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]], and [[Atlanta Falcons]]) and [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL) ([[Winnipeg Blue Bombers]]). Now, he is known for his inspirational speaking, sports marketing, and [[sports ministry]]. ==Early life== Perry Warren Tuttle was born on August 2, 1959, in [[Lexington, North Carolina]], to Russell Samuel and Betty Mae Tuttle. He attended [[North Davidson High School]] and was a standout player throughout his high school career. His successes in high school led to his recruitment by [[Clemson University]]. ==College career== The prime of Tuttle's football career was during his three seasons (1978–1981) at Clemson University. As of the 2018 season, Tuttle ranks ninth all-time in school history for touchdown receptions with 17, sixth all-time for receiving yards with 2,534, and tenth all-time for receptions with 150.[[Clemson Tigers football statistical leaders|Clemson Stat Leaders]]{{Circular reference|date=August 2019}} Tuttle caught the winning touchdown pass in the [[1982 Orange Bowl]], which secured the national championship for the Tigers. His celebration after the touchdown catch in the third quarter, arms outstretched above his head with ball in hand, made the cover of the January 11, 1982, edition of [[Sports Illustrated]] with the caption, “Orange Bowl Hero Perry Tuttle of Clemson.” In 1991, Clemson added Tuttle to their Hall of Fame, and in 1996, he was named as a member of Clemson's Centennial team. Later, in 1999, he was ranked by a panel of historians as the fourteenth-best player in Clemson football history.{{cite web |url=http://csusports.athleticsite.com/article.asp?articleID=257 |title=All-American Perry Tuttle brings message to CSU >> CSUsports.com |access-date=2008-11-19 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060529062815/http://csusports.athleticsite.com/article.asp?articleID=257 |archive-date=2006-05-29 }} ==Professional career== On April 27, 1982, Tuttle was selected in the first round (19th overall) of the [[NFL draft]] by the Buffalo Bills.{{cite news|url=https://buffalonews.com/sports/bills/erik-brady-perry-tuttle-bills-first-round-pick-40-years-ago-shares-hard-lessons-he/article_24af7666-c640-11ec-8d57-e77e4625b592.html|title=Perry Tuttle, Bills' first round pick 40 years ago, shares hard lessons he learned about fame|date=April 28, 2022|agency=[[The Buffalo News]]|author=Brady, Erik|accessdate=April 28, 2022|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20220428102036/https://buffalonews.com/sports/bills/erik-brady-perry-tuttle-bills-first-round-pick-40-years-ago-shares-hard-lessons-he/article_24af7666-c640-11ec-8d57-e77e4625b592.html|archivedate=April 28, 2022}} Tuttle spent two seasons with the Bills, producing 24 receptions for 368 yards and three touchdowns. After his two seasons in with the Bills, his career in the NFL took a major decline; while in Atlanta, he only played in five games which led to only minimal stat production, one reception for seven yards.{{Cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/T/TuttPe00.htm|title = Perry Tuttle Stats| website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]] }} In 1986, Tuttle began his six-season career in the Canadian Football League with the Winnipeg Blue Bombers. Throughout his time with the Bombers, he caught 321 passes for 5,817 yards and 41 touchdowns. On November 25, 1990, at [[BC Place Stadium]] in Vancouver, the Bombers defeated the [[Edmonton Eskimos]] 50–11 to win [[Grey Cup|the Grey Cup]]. In the third quarter of the game, Tuttle caught a 60-yard pass that later led to a five-yard touchdown catch.[[78th Grey Cup]] Two seasons after the Blue Bombers' championship win, Tuttle ended his football career and moved back to [[North Carolina]] (Charlotte). A few years after his retirement, Tuttle was once again recognized for his outstanding football talent with an induction into the Winnipeg Blue Bomber Hall of Fame.http://sportsillustrated.cnn.corn/features/1998/weekly/catchingup/1214{{dead link|date=March 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} ==Personal life== Tuttle's nephew [[Shy Tuttle]] plays in the NFL for the [[Carolina Panthers]] as a Defensive Tackle.{{Cite web |url=https://www.sbnation.com/college-football-recruiting/2014/3/6/5409670/shy-tuttle-recruit-scouting-report-north-carolina-defensive-tackle |title=Shy Tuttle recruit scouting report: Nimble North Carolina defensive tackle |last=Elliott |first=Bud |date=March 6, 2014 |website=SBNation.com |access-date=September 10, 2019}} ==References== {{1981 Clemson Tigers football navbox}} {{1982 NFL Draft}} {{Bills1982DraftPicks}} {{BillsFirstPick}} {{76th Grey Cup}} {{78th Grey Cup}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Tuttle, Perry}} [[Category:1959 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:American football wide receivers]] [[Category:Clemson Tigers football players]] [[Category:Buffalo Bills players]] [[Category:Atlanta Falcons players]] [[Category:Tampa Bay Buccaneers players]] [[Category:Winnipeg Blue Bombers players]] [[Category:Sportspeople from Lexington, North Carolina]] [[Category:Players of American football from North Carolina]]
